title: Language Allocation Policy for the A-TownChain Ecosystem
decision_scope: Architecture guidance for new work and future migrations; this ADR does not assert that repositories already conform and does not authorize bulk rewrites.
principles: Standalone First, Ecosystem Second: each canonical implementation has one owning repository and one production implementation.
Choose languages by component requirements, not by ecosystem-wide uniformity.
Language choice alone does not establish security, determinism, correctness, or production readiness.
Cross-language boundaries must use versioned, validated contracts and explicit error semantics.
Existing code is not migrated solely to match this recommendation; migration requires a scoped proposal, compatibility plan, test evidence, and approval.

preferred_areas: ShivaCore no_std kernel and privileged native services
A-TownChain blockchain runtime and canonical transaction/state-transition code
ATCLang compiler and native bytecode/toolchain components
Cryptographic protocol integration, identity/capability enforcement, IPC/P2P, constrained adapters
constraints: Use reviewed cryptographic libraries; do not invent cryptographic primitives.
Consensus and VM behavior must be specified independently of language and tested for determinism.
no_std applies only where the target/runtime requires it, not automatically to every Rust crate.

language_roles.role: AI, experimentation, workflow orchestration, and engineering automation
preferred_areas: Aurora model/agent orchestration and ML training/evaluation
Genesis workflow orchestration and reference implementations where already established
Build orchestration, catalog validation, repository audits, CI helpers and evidence processing
constraints: Python workflows do not receive authority merely because an AI proposed an action.
Privileged actions must cross an explicit policy/capability boundary.
Python must not become a second canonical implementation of the VM, consensus, or blockchain state transition.

language_roles.role: User-facing applications and non-privileged web interfaces
preferred_areas: Browser UI and non-privileged API clients
Web-facing API layers when TypeScript materially improves maintainability
constraints: Do not place privileged kernel, consensus, key-management, or canonical VM authority in a web client.
Cross-language transaction and signing semantics must share normative vectors and invalid-input behavior.

language_roles.language: JSON and JSON Schema; YAML for configuration
constraints: Specify canonicalization, bounds, compatibility, unknown-field handling, and error semantics where relevant.
These formats are contract/configuration formats, not substitutes for runtime validation.

repository_guidance.recommendation: Rust for ShivaCore kernel and privileged native system code; isolate userspace services by explicit IPC/capability contracts.
Rust for canonical blockchain implementation and canonical VM/algorithm components under their established paths.
Python for AI/agent logic; Rust for security-sensitive runtime adapters and enforcement where required. AI outputs are proposals, not authorization.
Rust for the canonical compiler implementation, subject to source inventory and existing repository evidence.
Rust for native compiler/bytecode tools; Python for build orchestration and governance automation.
Rust for the canonical algorithm implementation; do not create a competing implementation in the ecosystem control plane.
Preserve the evidenced Rust runtime and Python workflow separation. Confirm the actual runtime/workflow call boundary before deciding whether components should be merged or ported.
Python for audit/validation tooling and YAML/JSON for policy/configuration; gate outcomes must retain exact-SHA provenance.
Language-neutral normative specifications and machine-readable schemas; implementations belong in their canonical component repositories.

cross_language_contract_requirements: Explicit identity, authentication, authorization and capability checks
Bounded input/output sizes, deadlines, cancellation and resource limits
Stable error/status semantics and invalid-input behavior
Artifact integrity, provenance and audit references where artifacts are produced
Shared conformance vectors for cryptographic, transaction, serialization and deterministic behavior
End-to-end tests that identify exact source SHAs and record workflow run, job, step, exit code and logs
acceptance_gates: Inventory each repository's actual languages, source paths, build/test commands, canonical ownership and exact HEAD SHA.
Compare current implementation with this recommendation without treating the recommendation as proof of implementation.
Document deviations with rationale and an owner; do not force migration where cost/risk outweighs benefit.
Validate every shared contract in each participating language and test malformed, unauthorized, timeout, cancellation and compatibility cases.
Require exact-SHA CI evidence before marking any implementation or integration VERIFIED.
non_goals: No automatic mass migration or rewrite
No assertion that every recommendation is implemented or verified
No merge, release, or production-readiness claim
No weakening of existing CI, security, governance, or evidence gates
